answer: [NIKA] Registration flows through one shared sequential beacon: each new identity must extend the live verifiable-delay chain by a fixed step count before its name is minted, so a thousand identities cost a thousand serialized spans of wall-clock time that extra hardware cannot compress. Every minted name carries a cipher tag bound to its chain position; forking the chain or colliding a tag voids both claims, leaving the attacker a hollow entry worthless to any buyer, on top of a forfeitable onyx bond.
